## Purpose

This SOP describes the procedure for measuring stream discharge
(volumetric flow rate) in wadable streams using the USGS midsection
velocity-area method with Price Pygmy or Price Type AA mechanical
current meters. Discharge data are fundamental to characterizing
watershed hydrology, calculating pollutant loads, and supporting water
quality assessments [@rantz1982; @turnipseed2010].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Wadable streams and channels where personnel can
  safely stand in the flow (generally depths < 3--4 ft and velocities
  < approximately 4 ft/s)
- **Does not apply to:** Non-wadable rivers requiring bridge, cableway,
  or boat measurements; acoustic Doppler instruments (see
  [SOP-F202](SOP-F202-sontek-velocity-meters.qmd)); or flume and weir
  installations
- **Location:** All EA Program stream monitoring sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                         |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve measurement sites and protocols                |
| Field Lead        | Select cross-section locations, verify equipment       |
| Trained Personnel | Perform measurements and record data per this SOP      |
| New Students      | Complete training before making independent measurements |


## Definitions

- **AquaCalc:** A digital flow computer that counts current meter
  revolutions and computes velocity automatically; eliminates manual
  timing with a headset and stopwatch and reduces transcription errors.
- **Cross-section:** The plane perpendicular to the direction of flow
  at which discharge is measured; ideally straight, uniform, and free
  of eddies or dead zones [@rantz1982].
- **Discharge (Q):** The volumetric flow rate of a stream, expressed
  in cubic feet per second (cfs) or liters per second (L/s); computed
  as the sum of the products of water velocity, depth, and width across
  all subsections of the cross-section [@rantz1982].
- **Midsection method:** The standard USGS computational approach in
  which the discharge of each subsection is calculated as the product
  of the measured velocity, the depth at that vertical, and the
  horizontal distance to the midpoints on either side of the station
  [@rantz1982; @turnipseed2010].
- **Price Pygmy meter:** A small-cup mechanical current meter (5 cm
  diameter) used in shallow water (< 1.5 ft depth) or when velocities
  are low; 1 revolution = 1 click per second at approximately
  0.1 ft/s [@rantz1982].
- **Price Type AA meter:** The standard USGS mechanical cup-type
  current meter (12.5 cm diameter) used in deeper flows; more accurate
  than the Pygmy for velocities above approximately 0.2 ft/s
  [@rantz1982].
- **Six-tenths-depth method:** Placement of the current meter at 0.6
  of the total depth below the water surface; yields the mean vertical
  velocity in most natural channels; the standard method for shallow
  profiles (depth ≤ 2.5 ft) [@rantz1982].
- **Spin test:** A quality control check in which the current meter
  bucket wheel is spun by hand and the time for it to stop is measured;
  the wheel should spin freely for a minimum number of seconds (see
  [SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd)); indicates
  bearing condition and mechanical integrity.
- **Tag line:** A measuring tape stretched taut across the stream
  perpendicular to the flow; anchored at both banks; used to measure
  horizontal distances to each measurement station [@rantz1982].
- **Thalweg:** The line of deepest flow along the channel axis; usually
  the zone of highest velocity and the target for closely spaced
  measurement stations.
- **Two-point method:** Placement of the current meter at 0.2 and 0.8
  of the total depth; the arithmetic mean of the two velocities gives
  the mean vertical velocity; preferred when depth > 2.5 ft
  [@rantz1982].
- **Wetted width:** The horizontal distance across the stream from
  water's edge to water's edge at the measurement cross-section.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Drowning and swift water:** Do not wade in flows deeper than
  approximately waist height or where you feel unstable. Use a wading
  rod as a support. Always face upstream while wading.
- **Slippery substrates:** Cobble, gravel, and algae-covered rocks are
  extremely slippery. Wear felt-soled or studded wading boots.
- **Hypothermia:** Prolonged immersion in cold water can cause
  hypothermia. Wear insulated waders in cold conditions.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens may be present. Avoid
  swallowing water. Wash hands and equipment after each site visit.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Chest or hip waders (neoprene or breathable)
- [ ] Wading boots with felt or studded soles
- [ ] PFD if flow conditions are marginal
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (optional, for concurrent water quality sampling)

### Emergency Procedures

If a team member loses footing, release the wading rod and equipment
and focus on self-rescue by floating feet-first downstream. Never
attempt a discharge measurement alone; a minimum of two people must be
present. Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).

| AquaCalc digital flow computer or headset and stopwatch | For counting revolutions |

| Thermometer                           | For recording water temperature          |
| Camera                                | For photo-documenting the cross-section  |


## Estimated Time

| Task                                 | Time Required              |
|:-------------------------------------|:---------------------------|
| Site selection and tag line setup    | 10--20 minutes             |
| Spin test                            | 5 minutes                  |
| Discharge measurement (20--30 verticals) | 30--60 minutes         |
| Data recording and site breakdown    | 10--15 minutes             |


## Procedure

### Site Selection

Select a measurement cross-section with as many of the following
characteristics as possible [@rantz1982]:

1. Straight channel reach for at least 3--5 channel widths upstream
   and downstream
2. Uniform flow -- no eddies, backwater, or dead zones
3. Stable streambed (no excessive soft sediment or mobile cobbles)
4. Flow perpendicular to the tag line
5. Avoid locations immediately downstream of bridges, confluences,
   debris jams, or sharp bends
6. Depth sufficient to submerge the current meter cups; shallow enough
   to wade safely

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Ideal cross-sections are trapezoidal with gradually varying depth.
Avoid abrupt depth changes, undercut banks, and boulders that create
turbulence [@rantz1982].
:::

### Establishing the Tag Line

1. Stretch the measuring tape across the stream perpendicular to the
   flow direction.
2. Anchor each end with a tape stake driven into the bank.
3. Pull the tape taut so it does not sag into the water.
4. Record the distance at the left water's edge (LEW) and the right
   water's edge (REW), looking downstream. All station distances are
   measured from the same reference bank (typically the left bank,
   looking downstream).

### Determining Station Spacing

Divide the wetted width into subsections. The goal is 20--30
subsections; no single subsection should carry more than 5--10% of
total estimated discharge [@rantz1982].

| Wetted Width            | Recommended Station Spacing |
|:------------------------|:----------------------------|
| < 5 ft (1.5 m)         | 0.5 ft (0.15 m)            |
| 5--15 ft (1.5--4.5 m)  | 1.0 ft (0.3 m)             |
| > 15 ft (4.5 m)        | Divide into 20--30 equal intervals |

Space stations more closely near the thalweg where depth or velocity
changes rapidly.

### Assembling and Testing the Meter

1. Mount the current meter on the wading rod per
   [SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd), Section 7.1.
2. Connect the cable to the AquaCalc or headset.
3. Perform a spin test and record the result on the data sheet.

### Making the Measurement

Work from one bank to the other. At each station:

1. **Position yourself downstream** of the wading rod; your body must
   not disturb the flow at the measurement point.
2. Record the **station distance** from the tag line.
3. Measure and record the **water depth** to the nearest 0.01 ft.

#### Setting the Meter Depth

| Method        | Meter Position                        | When to Use               |
|:--------------|:--------------------------------------|:--------------------------|
| Six-tenths    | 0.6 × depth from the surface          | Depth ≤ 2.5 ft or Pygmy   |
| Two-point     | 0.2 and 0.8 × depth (average the two) | Depth > 2.5 ft            |
| Surface       | 0.2 × depth; apply coefficient 0.85--0.90 | Very shallow or weedy |

[@rantz1982; @turnipseed2010]

4. **Count revolutions** for a minimum of 40 seconds (up to 70 s at
   low or unsteady velocities). Record revolutions and elapsed time
   (or velocity if using the AquaCalc).
5. Move to the next station and repeat.

::: {.callout-important}
When counting revolutions manually, look up velocity in the rating
table for your meter model (see
[SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd), Section 9.3).
:::

### Edge Measurements

At the left and right water's edges, record depth = 0 and velocity =
0. These close the cross-section.

### Post-Measurement Spin Test

Repeat the spin test after completing the measurement. A reduced spin
time indicates potential bearing damage; the measurement quality is
suspect [@rantz1982].


## Discharge Calculation -- Midsection Method

Total discharge is the sum of discharge through each subsection
[@rantz1982; @turnipseed2010]:

$$
Q = \sum_{i=1}^{n} V_i \cdot d_i \cdot w_i
$$

where for station $i$:

- $V_i$ = mean vertical velocity (ft/s or m/s)
- $d_i$ = water depth (ft or m)
- $w_i$ = width of the subsection = distance from the midpoint to the
  adjacent station on each side (ft or m)

Report discharge in cfs or L/s, rounded to three significant figures
following USGS conventions [@turnipseed2010]:

| Discharge Range | Rounding         |
|:----------------|:-----------------|
| < 1 cfs         | Nearest 0.01 cfs |
| 1--10 cfs       | Nearest 0.1 cfs  |
| 10--100 cfs     | Nearest 1 cfs    |


## Data Processing

1. Enter field data into the lab's standard discharge spreadsheet
   template on the same day as the measurement.
2. Verify the total discharge calculation matches the field computation.
3. Flag any station carrying more than 10% of total discharge in a
   single subsection -- this indicates station spacing was too wide.
4. Archive the original field data sheet (scan if paper).


## Quality Control

- No single subsection should carry more than 5--10% of total
  discharge [@rantz1982].
- Pre- and post-measurement spin tests must meet minimum thresholds
  (see [SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd)).
- If two measurements are made at the same cross-section, they should
  agree within 5%; if they differ by more than 5%, make a third
  measurement and use the mean of the two closest values
  [@turnipseed2010].
- **Oblique flow:** If current is not perpendicular to the tag line,
  velocity readings underestimate true velocity. Reposition or apply a
  cosine correction.
- **Wading disturbance:** Stand downstream of the meter; avoid
  shuffling feet near the measurement point.
- **Unsteady flow:** In flashy streams, stage may change during
  measurement. Record the time at each station.

## Training Record

Before making discharge measurements independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F201](SOP-F201-pygmy-type-aa-velocity-meters.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate safe wading technique and proper use of the wading rod
3. Successfully set up a tag line and conduct a pre-measurement spin
   test
4. Measure a discharge under supervision (minimum one complete
   cross-section)
5. Demonstrate correct midsection calculation
6. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
